parsed.explanation: The quote is accurate: the §3 dichotomy literally lists only g≡0 and the mixed case 'both values attainable', so the pure case V={c}, c>0 is not named. But the omission is repaired in the text itself. Sections 4–6 never use S₀≠∅: Lemma 1 requires only S_c≠∅ (its case d=0 is exactly b=c), and the covering argument derives S₀=∅ vacuously if S₀ was already empty. Section 7 then concludes 'Since S₀=∅ … Together with §3 this forces g(x)≡c … Thus f(x)=x+c (c>0)', which is precisely the omitted case, and the Verification covers every c≥0. So the necessity argument establishes g constant in all cases; the non-exhaustive phrasing is a presentational slip, not a mathematical error or gap.
